lenses.description: the newest lens step count per package eid declared in the app's store, kept across code rollbacks so current pages use the current vocabulary path

worker.description: the worker its serving release built, as that release's deploy.worker says: empty when it built none, so a page asks the dispatch namespace for nothing; absent where no release recorded it

access.description: public: anyone reads. open: anyone writes. private: only members

draft.description: the draft its edits since the served release belong to: the written rows carrying it are those edits

fence.description: the token holding edits while a release copies its selected draft

followed.description: the app's preview link, kept across deploys: each write to its draft, and each deploy, is told to the link's pages

store.description: the immutable handle its storage and runtime use, independent of its current address

files.description: the app-owned bucket prefix, independent of its address and served source

blobs.description: the bucket prefix its uploads are kept under, written once at birth with its store, so an app given a store it did not make keeps the bytes that store names

app.description: one app in a space: its slug, the version currently served, and who may open it

source.description: the source release this installed copy came from

message.description: everything this release changed and why, as whoever released it wrote it, the way a commit message says it; agents working the app read it before changing it

reload.description: a contract change: pages crossing this release must reload; absent derives the level from files

lenses.description: the app's newest lens step count per package when this release was made, which a page of a release that records no speaks reads its session step from; absent on releases made before version capture

speaks.description: the lens step per package this release's pages speak: its own vocabulary's steps and the session step it shipped with, recorded at deploy so a page's request reads no vocabulary file; absent on releases made before it was recorded

deploy.description: one release of an app: the files it shipped, and the worker built from them

last_deploy.description: who last put a release of this app live, and when: a deploy or a rollback. by is the actor (a person, or an agent writing for one), via its session

acts_for.description: an agent writing for a person (a connector client, the CLI), named for itself in doc.title: the actor its deploys and the apps it makes are stamped with, never the person

name.description: the domain, as a person typed it; one hostname points at one place

serves.description: what the name opens: a space, whose front page it opens at `/` with every app at `/<app>/`, or a single app, which it opens at `/`

to.description: another hostname of the same place that this one sends every visitor to, path and query kept, with a 301: the bare domain sending its visitors to www; absent where this hostname serves the place itself

stage.description: pending while it is being set up, active once it serves, error if it cannot

verification.description: Cloudflare's ownership TXT record for this attachment, retained after Cloudflare activates it; empty while provisioning

at.description: when the stage was last written

hostname.description: a domain somebody owns, and the one place it serves

sandboxed.description: when the space's owner put the copy in a sandbox, a browser origin of its own; empty while it runs like the space's own apps

trusted.description: the inverse sandbox mark kept in step for rollback readers

installed.description: a copy of somebody else’s app, at the version it was copied from

trend.description: What an app or a space counted, by day, for its charts: the last thirty days, a quiet day absent.

requests.description: Requests by day, YYYY-MM-DD, as Cloudflare's analytics said at the hourly reading.

spend.description: Dollars spent from the space's budget by day, YYYY-MM-DD, added as each is spent: models, builds, generated media, voice and texts.

sources.description: The same dollars by what sold them, each a day map like `spend`: a model provider (`anthropic`, `openai`, `workers-ai`, `openrouter`), `voice`, `texts`, `browser`, or `models` for a model call that named no provider.

paid.description: The part of `spend` a space paying for its plan covered, by day; the rest the platform gave.

month.description: the month it counts, as YYYY-MM

models.description: dollars spent on models this month, each call weighed by its model's price

drawn.description: dollars models, voice and texts have spent, every month together

ws_hibernated.description: hibernated WebSocket requests counted this month

visits.description: an app's page views over the last 30 days, as the hourly reading found them

files.description: bytes held in uploaded files and application files

realtime.description: dollars spent on realtime models this month

texts.description: dollars spent on its apps' text messages this month

visitors.description: dollars of models, voice and texts this month spent for its apps' visitors, already counted in each

refunded.description: dollars of models, voice and texts this month the platform refunded, off what the month spent and off drawn

credit.description: dollars of this month's models, voice and texts past the space's budget, drawn from its credit

meter.description: what a space used in one month

tier.description: free, plus or pro: the tier every ceiling the space meets is read from

customer.description: the Stripe customer the space pays as

subscription.description: the Stripe subscription behind the tier

status.description: that subscription's status as Stripe last said it (`active`, `past_due`, `canceled`, …), mirrored by the webhook and never moved by anything here: Stripe's state machine, not ours

until.description: when the paid-for period runs out

ending.description: when a subscription that will not renew stops paying

at.description: when the Stripe event the row was derived from was created

plan.description: what a space pays for: a function of one Stripe subscription, derived whole from it on every webhook. The platform writes it and no client can.

cap.description: the most dollars the space's owner lets it spend past its monthly budget in a month, which is also the most credit it may hold for one month: 0 until they choose one

bought.description: dollars of credit ever bought, each block paid before it is spent

spent.description: dollars of credit ever spent; what is left of bought carries to the next month

credit.description: AI credit a space buys in blocks and spends past its monthly model and voice budget, up to a cap its owner sets (meter.ts `creditOf`). The platform writes it: the cap through the plan settings' door, the rest in the directory's own transaction as a block is paid for and as a spend goes past the budget.

published.description: the name and version this app appears under in the gallery

report.description: where somebody stood when they said something was wrong: the app, its deployed version and the platform's release, on a report an app filed about itself or a support thread feedback opened

tool.description: the name of the tool the call asked for, as it is published

source.description: the call it refused, wherever that is recorded; one call is one occurrence however many boundaries it crossed

space.description: the space the call was made in, where that is known

session.description: the session or run that made the call, where that is known

release.description: the platform release that refused it

tool_refusal.description: one time a yaks.app tool refused a call, worn with the call's `refusal{code}` and its cause as `content{body}`: the words of the refusal with the values in them taken out. It keeps no arguments. Never a bug: refusals reach TaskMaster in an hourly `refusal_report`, and one counted in a delivered report is deleted 30 days after it was refused

refusal_report.description: an hour's letter to TaskMaster grouping the tool refusals counted in it by tool, code and cause, worn with the letter's `doc{title, body}`, `mail` and `deliver`; `delivered{at}` once it has left

counted.description: the `refusal_report` a tool refusal was counted in; one without it waits for the next report, and is never deleted

person.description: the signed-in person whose thread this is, from the caller's credential; absent on a thread opened signed out, which nobody but the platform reads

session.description: the run it was said from: the Operator session or the connector's instrument the credential vouched for

call.description: the tool call it was said in, where the door recorded one

agent.description: the connector client it was said through, by the name it gave at connect: the platform's answers ride that client's next tool result, across reconnects (workers/yak/support-reply.ts); absent from an Operator or a browser

support.description: who a support thread or one of its messages came from, as the caller's credential said: ownership on a thread (a conversation{} wearing report{}), evidence on each of its comment{} messages. A message without it is the platform's answer (workers/yak/support.ts).

paired.description: when the person typed the screen's code

at.description: when the screen took the pairing up; absent while the person's code waits for a screen to claim it

screen.description: a TV or any screen paired, read-only, with one person by the code it showed (RFC 8628): it shows whatever draft that person's agent is building. Its eid is derived from the code, so nothing is written until the person pairs it

email.description: the address the code was mailed to

phone.description: the US mobile number the code was texted to, in E.164 form; set instead of `email`

from.description: on a texted code, who asked: a mac of the address the request came from, so texts per visitor are counted

unsent.description: why the letter or text carrying the code never left, as its sender said; absent while it went or is still going

signin.description: a sign-in in progress: the code mailed or texted out, when it expires, how many tries are left, and why its letter never left when it did not

store.description: the immutable handle its storage uses, independent of its current address

space.description: one customer’s area of the platform, at its own slug

written.description: One file written into an app's draft: its path, the SHA-256 naming the bytes the write left there (stored once, under that address), or none where the write deleted it, the SHA-256 of what it replaced, and who wrote it when. A draft is the newest of these per path among the rows carrying it, and every row for a path is that path's history.

draft.description: the app's draft when it was written

path.description: the file's path from the app's root

sha.description: the SHA-256 of the bytes; absent where the write deleted the file

was.description: the SHA-256 of the bytes the write replaced; absent where there was no file

switched.description: One move of an app's live pointer between kept deploys; source keeps the immutable serving bytes selected at that moment.

comp.description: a revocable plan granted by the platform, independent of any subscription
